subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu DM sessions rebuilt after gateway restart — duplicate keys + maintenance pruning

question: Which Feishu DM session-continuity repair should OpenClaw adopt before implementation: TTL-aware direct-DM protection plus Feishu `open_id` validation/doctor repair, blanket direct-DM protection, or treating `per-account-channel-peer` as the supported workaround only?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the durable fix changes retention policy and possibly existing session-key history; automation should not choose the unbounded-growth, validation, and migration tradeoff without maintainer intent.

options.title: TTL-aware retention plus Feishu repair
options.body: Protect active or recently used direct DM sessions, validate Feishu direct peer ids at the plugin boundary, and add doctor or migration handling for malformed/duplicate Feishu keys.

options.title: Blanket-protect direct DMs
options.body: Treat all direct DM session rows as protected maintenance entries, accepting larger long-term stores to avoid unexpected DM session eviction.

options.title: Document workaround only
options.body: Keep `per-account-channel-peer` as the supported multi-account workaround and leave maintenance pruning plus malformed-id cleanup to operators for now.

recommendation.title: TTL-aware retention plus Feishu repair
recommendation.body: Protect active or recently used direct DM sessions, validate Feishu direct peer ids at the plugin boundary, and add doctor or migration handling for malformed/duplicate Feishu keys.

likelyOwner.reason: The central unresolved choice is in the session-store maintenance policy, where steipete has the strongest recent code-history signal.
